s: September 28, 2024 - X logical font description (XLFD) is a font standard used by the X Window System and first published in 1988. Modern X software typically relies on the newer Fontconfig system instead, but XLFDs are still supported in current X window implementations for compatibility with legacy software.

t: X Logical Font Description Conventions
s: XLFD is divided into two basic components: the FontName, which gives all font information needed to uniquely identify a font in X protocol requests (for example, OpenFont, ListFonts, and so on) and a variable list of optional FontProperties, which describe a font in more detail.

s: The X Window System uses Logical Font Descriptions instead of font names. Since font names are not in fact logical, this doesn't work very well, and frankly ends up in a mess. None the less, if you download this short shell script, xlfd, and run chmod +x xlfd, you can use it to list fonts.
